item.content:encoded:
Hideki Matsui is heading back to the most iconic franchise in Japanese baseball, and the move is giving collectors a new reason to revisit one of the hobby’s most important modern international careers.
The Yomiuri Giants introduced Matsui as their new manager on October 23, placing one of the most accomplished stars in Japanese baseball history back at the center of the team where he first became a national sensation. For collectors, the news does more than reconnect Matsui to the Giants. It adds another layer of historical meaning to his rookie cards, home run commemoratives, and Giants-era collectibles.
Matsui’s playing career already carried major hobby relevance on both sides of the Pacific. He was a slugging superstar for Yomiuri before becoming a marquee MLB name with the New York Yankees and later playing for the Angels, A’s, and Rays. Now, with a return to the Giants in a leadership role, his cardboard legacy gains another chapter tied directly to the club that first made him famous.
Why Matsui’s Return Matters to Collectors
The Yomiuri Giants are not just another team in Nippon Professional Baseball. They are one of the most recognized and most scrutinized organizations in Japan, with a national fan base and a history that reaches deep into the culture of the sport. Managing the Giants is widely viewed as one of the highest-profile jobs in Japanese sports, which means Matsui’s appointment immediately carries weight far beyond a standard coaching change.
For more collector background, read Top 3 Gale Sayers Cards Ever: His Most Valuable and Iconic Football Issues.
That prominence matters in the hobby. Collectors often place additional value on cards when a player’s legacy expands beyond playing accomplishments alone. Hall of Fame elections, milestone anniversaries, championships, awards, and managerial appointments can all shift how collectors view an athlete’s career arc. Matsui’s return to Yomiuri fits that pattern because it connects his playing days, his cultural importance, and the legacy of the Giants in a single storyline.
For longtime collectors of Japanese baseball cards, Matsui already stood as one of the cornerstone names of the 1990s and early 2000s. For newer buyers, this managerial move may serve as an entry point into a market that includes BBM, Takara, Calbee, and a unique run of home run-related issues tied directly to his career achievements.
The Shigeo Nagashima Connection Adds Historical Weight
Matsui’s return also resonates because of his close connection to Shigeo Nagashima, one of the most beloved figures in Japanese baseball history. Nagashima spent his entire playing career with the Giants from 1958 through 1974, batting .305 with 444 home runs. He later managed the club from 1975 to 1980 and again from 1993 to 2001, overlapping with Matsui’s Giants playing career.
Known widely as “Mr. Giants” and “Mr. Pro Yakyu,” Nagashima was far more than a former star. He was a symbol of the sport in Japan. After his death at age 89 on June 3, 2025, many fans found meaning in the timing and numerology surrounding the date, connecting it to his uniform number 3 and his place at third base. The emotional significance of his passing only deepened the importance of the players and stories most closely tied to him.
Matsui was one of those players. At Nagashima’s funeral, family remarks underscored just how much Matsui meant to the former Giants legend. Matsui also shared a story from their years together, recalling that he once asked about playing third base, only to be told that his place was in the outfield. Nagashima told him, “I want you to be Joe DiMaggio.”
That anecdote became even more meaningful later, when Matsui visited Nagashima’s home for swing work and saw a DiMaggio bat and a large image of the Yankees legend. Matsui came to understand exactly what Nagashima had in mind for him as a player. When the time came for Matsui to leave Japan for Major League Baseball, he referenced that conversation, telling his manager that if he was supposed to be Joe DiMaggio, then he was going to the Yankees.
Now that Matsui is returning to guide the Giants, collectors are not just looking at a former slugger taking a new job. They are looking at a major figure stepping into a role tied to one of the most important mentor-student relationships in Japanese baseball history.
Matsui’s Career Resume Still Drives Strong Hobby Interest
Matsui’s on-field record already gave him a strong collector base before the managerial news. Drafted by the Giants out of high school, he played for Yomiuri from 1993 through 2002 and hit 332 home runs for the club. He won three MVP awards in Japan and became one of the defining power hitters of his era there.
He then moved to MLB and added 175 more home runs while playing for the Yankees, Angels, A’s, and Rays. His most famous moment in the United States came with New York, where he earned 2009 World Series MVP honors. That blend of Japanese stardom and MLB success gives Matsui broader appeal than many players whose card markets are concentrated mainly in one country.
His total of 507 professional home runs between Japan and MLB also created the basis for one of the more unusual long-running card concepts attached to any modern player.
The NTV Home Run Cards Stand Out as a Signature Matsui Collectible
Among Matsui’s most distinctive issues is the Nippon Television home run card run celebrating each of his 507 career home runs. The series began in 1993 and continued throughout his career, creating a visual archive of his power production across different stages of his baseball life.
These cards are notable because they are built around specific home run moments. Rather than functioning as generic commemorative issues, the photographs show actual scenes connected to each blast, such as Matsui at the plate or circling the bases. For player collectors, that gives the run a documentary feel that is hard to replicate with standard base cards or later tribute releases.
The concept also gives Matsui collectors a built-in long-term chase. A single card is interesting. A complete run of 507 tells the story of his entire power career. That kind of project appeals to advanced player collectors who value completeness, chronology, and visual storytelling as much as rarity.
A collection of all of the NTV home run cards is displayed at the Matsui Hideki Baseball Museum in Ishikawa Prefecture, along with other memorabilia from his career. That museum presence further supports the importance of the set within the larger record of Matsui’s legacy.
Key Hideki Matsui Rookie Cards to Know
For many collectors, the first stop remains Matsui’s rookie-year cards from 1993. His best-known Japanese rookie is card #423 in the 1993 BBM set, a release that also includes Ichiro Suzuki’s rookie. That pairing has long made the set especially notable among modern Japanese issues.
While Ichiro’s card in the set frequently commands a significantly higher price, Matsui’s BBM rookie has remained relatively accessible compared with his stature in the sport. Reported market levels place raw or lower-grade examples around the $30 range, making it one of the more approachable key cards for a player of Matsui’s stature.
Collectors do need to watch for one important detail. A reprint of the 1993 BBM Matsui rookie was later included in the 2002 BBM “The Legend of Hideki Matsui” set. The reprint is marked “REPRINT” on the back, which provides a clear distinction, but it is still a point buyers should verify before purchasing an ungraded example.
Two other rookie-year cards from 1993 are also important for Matsui collectors:
- 1993 Takara Hideki Matsui
- 1993 Calbee Hideki Matsui
Recent reported sales cited for those cards included a PSA 8 Takara at $120 and a PSA 6 Calbee at $95. Those figures do not define the entire market, but they do show steady demand for Matsui’s Japanese rookie-year material, particularly when graded examples surface.
MLB Rookie-Year Appeal Still Matters
Matsui’s collecting profile is not limited to his Japan-issued cards. He also has a wide range of 2003 MLB rookie-year cards showing him in Yankees uniform, a category that continues to hold crossover appeal for both Japanese baseball collectors and mainstream MLB hobby buyers.
The Yankees connection remains especially important. Matsui was already a massive name when he arrived in the majors, and his New York years gave him a much larger international cardboard footprint through major U.S. manufacturers. Upper Deck and Topps both played a role in cards linked to his major league years, including home run-related issues and standard MLB releases.
That means the market for Matsui cards operates on two tracks at once. One track is rooted in Japanese issues, especially his 1993 rookie-year cards and the NTV home run series. The other is built around the visibility and collector familiarity of his Yankees-era cards. His return to the Giants may benefit both sides of that market, since renewed attention to his career often sends collectors searching across all phases of a player’s catalog.
Cards and Storylines Collectors May Watch Next
One of the more interesting hobby angles going forward is the possibility of new Japanese cards showing Matsui not as a player, but as the Giants’ manager. That distinction can matter more than it sounds. Collectors often respond strongly to first-year cards tied to a new role, particularly when the subject is a franchise legend returning to an iconic team.
Matsui will wear number 90 as Giants manager, the same number Nagashima wore when he began his own managerial run with the club. That detail strengthens the symbolic link between the two men and could become an especially meaningful note for collectors if future card issues highlight the continuity.
For player collectors, the most likely areas of increased attention include:
- 1993 BBM #423, especially original copies rather than the 2002 reprint
- 1993 Takara and 1993 Calbee rookies, particularly graded examples
- NTV home run cards, either singles tied to milestone blasts or longer runs
- 2003 Yankees rookie-year cards, which connect his Japanese stardom to his MLB arrival
- Future manager-era Japanese issues, if they are released with strong Giants branding or tribute themes
Collectors who favor legacy-driven markets often respond when a player’s story becomes easier to tell in full. Matsui now checks multiple boxes in that regard: Yomiuri icon, MLB success story, World Series MVP, student of Shigeo Nagashima, and now manager of Japan’s most prominent franchise.
What to Keep in Mind Before Buying
As attention rises, collectors should stay selective. Condition remains critical, especially for 1990s Japanese issues that can vary significantly in centering, edge wear, and surface quality. Authentication of reprints versus originals is also essential, particularly with the 1993 BBM rookie. Graded examples may offer more confidence, but raw cards can still be appealing if the seller provides clear front-and-back images.
It is also worth separating broad interest from immediate price spikes. Matsui’s market may gain momentum because of the managerial news, but the most durable value usually sits with cards that already matter historically: true rookie-year issues, scarce or iconic player-specific sets, and cards tied to signature career achievements.
For Matsui, that means his foundation remains strong. The 1993 BBM rookie anchors his Japanese card story. The Takara and Calbee issues provide alternate rookie-year paths. The 507-home run NTV run offers one of the most distinctive player collecting challenges in the sport. And his Yankees-era releases connect him to one of baseball’s largest global collecting audiences.
With Matsui back in a Giants uniform, this time in the dugout rather than the batter’s box, collectors have a fresh reason to revisit a career that already carried significance in two baseball worlds.

item.content:encoded:
Cards
Former MLB, Japanese star Hideki Matsui a Giant again, giving his top cards historical significance
It had been the hope of Japanese baseball legend Shigeo Nagashima that Hideki Matsui would one day return to manage his beloved Yomiuri Giants.
Nagashima, who was known as “Mr. Giants,” “Mr. Pro Yakyu” (Pro Baseball) and simply “Mister,” played for the Yomiuri Giants his entire career, from 1958-74. He pleased the crowd by playing the game with much flair and teamed with slugger Sadaharu Oh to win championship after championship. After retiring with a .305 average and 444 home runs, Nagashima managed the Giants from 1975-1980 and then again, this time with Matsui on the team, from 1993-2001.
Related Content:
Nagashima is widely considered the most popular baseball player ever in Japan. When he died at the age of 89 on June 3, 2025, there were even some who found special meaning in the specific time and date that Nagashima died, which was on 6/3 at 6:39 in the morning. All of these numbers are divisible by 3, Shigeo’s uniform number as a player. Not only that, but Nagashima played third base. Fans also pointed out that the age Nagashima lived to, 89, must be symbolic, since one way to read the number 8 in Japanese is “ya,” and the number 9 is “kyu.” Put the 8 and 9 together, and you get the word for baseball, “yakyu.”
At Nagashima’s funeral, his daughter Mina said that her father “loved Matsui more than anything in the world,” and then added, “I have seriously thought that if Mr. Matsui and I were drowning in the sea at the same time, my father would save Mr. Matsui first.”
Mina remembered that when Matsui retired at the age of 38, her father remarked that he retired at 38, just like Matsui. “He appeared a little sad,” Mina said, describing the moment. “But there was also a look of pride on his face.”
Matsui traveled from his home in the States for the funeral in Japan, and in his speech he told a story about asking his manager if he could try playing third base. Nagashima, the former third baseman, told Matsui that without question his place was to be in the outfield. “I want you to be Joe DiMaggio,” Nagashima said.
At first, Matsui did not get the meaning of this statement. But on a later occasion, when Matsui went to Nagashima’s house to practice his swing, he saw a bat of DiMaggio and a large photo of Joltin’ Joe.
“I then understood that Mister really liked DiMaggio,” Matsui said. “I was happy that he told me that he wanted me to be that kind of player.”
When Matsui decided to head to the big leagues, he knew it would be a great disappointment for Nagashima. “Manager, you said Joe DiMaggio,” Matsui said when he went to see Nagashima. “So I am going to the Yankees.”
At this, Matsui received a big smile from Nagashima, and when Matsui saw that smile he finally thought, although it was difficult, that after all it would be okay to leave the Giants. But later Nagashima looked forward to the day that Matsui would come back.
The Giants introduced Matsui, 52, as their new manager on October 23. It might be called the most high-profile job in sports in Japan. The Giants are the most historically great and polarizing team in Nippon Professional Baseball. Giants fans are by no means limited to Tokyo but are everywhere in the country.
Matsui was drafted by the Giants out of high school and went on to slam 332 home runs over 10 years with the team, from 1993-2002. Matsui hit 175 more homers in his major league career with the Yankees, Angels, A’s, and Rays. He won three MVP awards in Japan and was the 2009 World Series MVP with the Yankees.
A Nippon Television (NTV) card set celebrating each of his 507 home runs was issued throughout his career, starting in 1993 (the major league home run cards were made by Upper Deck and then later Topps). The photos on these unique cards actually show a moment from each of his home runs, whether it is Matsui at the plate or rounding the bases. A collection of NTV cards of all of the home runs is displayed, along with other Matsui memorabilia, at the Matsui Hideki Baseball Museum, which is operated by Hideki’s family and located in Ishikawa prefecture.
Matsui’s main Japanese rookie card is #423 in the 1993 BBM set, which also contains Ichiro Suzuki’s rookie. While Ichiro’s rookie often sells for $200 dollars or more, Matsui’s can be had for around $30. Just be careful when buying one, as there is a reprint of the card that is part of a 2002 BBM “The Legend of Hideki Matsui” set. This card is clearly marked “REPRINT” on the back.
Two other 1993 rookie cards were made by Takara and Calbee, and there are many 2003 major league rookie cards of Matsui in Yankees threads. Recent sales of the 1993 cards include a Takara graded PSA 8 for $120 and a Calbee graded PSA 6 for $95.
Now Giants fans will get to see Hideki in a Giants uniform once again, and collectors will have a chance at Japanese cards of Matsui as a manager. He will wear number 90, the same number that Nagashima wore when he started out as manager of the Giants.
— SCD contributor Matt Bosch lived in Japan and went to his first professional baseball game in Japan 20 years ago and has been a fan ever since. He taught at a university in Japan and enjoys researching and writing about Japanese baseball."

item.content:encoded:
Hideki Matsui is going back to Yomiuri with a different job. The former Yankees star has been introduced as the Japanese club’s new manager, MLB’s Max Ralph reported Friday.
New York quickly offered its congratulations. In a message posted by the Yankees, the club wished Matsui well in his new chapter with the team where he spent all 10 seasons of his Japanese playing career.
A Yankees favorite returns to his first baseball home
Yankees fans know the October version of Matsui best. He won the 2009 World Series MVP award after going 8-for-13 with three home runs and eight RBIs against Philadelphia. That was the finish to seven seasons in New York, from 2003 through 2009.
But Yomiuri isn’t a sentimental stop on the way to some other job. Matsui was already a major star there before joining the Yankees. His move into the dugout brings him back to the organization where he won three Central League MVP awards and three Japan Series titles as a player.
That history helps explain the attention around this appointment. He isn’t arriving as a familiar name with no connection to the club. He knows what wearing that uniform meant long before his years in the Bronx.
The playing record is secure; managing is a new assignment
Matsui finished his major-league career with 175 home runs and an .822 OPS over 10 seasons. Those numbers establish what he did with a bat. They don’t tell us how he’ll handle a struggling player, balance a lineup or make a late-game decision from the bench.
That’s what makes the move more interesting than another ceremonial appearance. He’ll have responsibility for other players’ opportunities and for decisions that don’t come with the immediate feedback of his own at-bats.
For clarity, this is a Yomiuri appointment, not a Yankees coaching move or evidence of a change to New York’s staff. The Yankees are celebrating a former champion taking on a new job. Matsui now gets the much less ceremonial work of managing the club that first made him a star.

item.content:encoded:
ゴジラの帰還が、巨人に〝世界規模の夢〟をもたらす。巨人は２３日、松井秀喜新監督（５２）の就任を正式発表。都内のホテルで山口寿一オーナーと会見した新指揮官は、２４年ぶりに古巣へ復帰し、背番号「９０」のユニホームに袖を通した。注目は采配だけではない。ＭＬＢで築いた規格外の人脈が、名だたるメジャーリーガーの大型補強や超豪華な指導陣を呼び寄せる可能性が出始めている。
日米通算５０７本塁打の大スターが古巣の命運を背負う。「今日は満面の笑顔で自分の故郷に戻ってきたつもりです」。松井監督は就任会見で、そう語り「これからのジャイアンツに新たな黄金時代が訪れるよう、今日ここからスタートしていきたい」と宣言した。
山口オーナーも「強いジャイアンツにしていくには、松井監督にお願いするしかない」と期待を込めた。契約は３年。恩師・長嶋茂雄氏が監督時代に着けた「９０」を背負い、３０日から始まる秋季キャンプで本格始動する。「指導者の経験はほぼありません」と自ら認めたが、手持ちのカードが乏しいわけではない。
新体制の最大の武器となり得るのが、現役、引退後の２０年以上で培った〝ＭＬＢ人脈〟だ。松井監督はヤンキースのＧＭ特別アドバイザーとして１２年間、傘下の若手育成に尽力。現主将兼主砲のアーロン・ジャッジ外野手もマイナー時代の教え子。２０１５年には打撃の体の使い方を直接伝授した。
ならば将来的にジャッジが選手として、師匠が新指揮官となった巨人のユニホームに袖を通したら――。実現すれば、球界騒然の超大型補強だ。一方、ヤンキース時代に親交を深めた元主将デレク・ジーター氏や、０９年の世界一をともに味わったアレックス・ロドリゲス氏ら大物ＯＢには、臨時コーチ就任や将来の入閣という夢も膨らむ。
松井監督は会見で「選手が自分自身で成長できるように」と力説した。米球界の練習法やデータ活用を巨人流に取り込み、若手が自ら課題を克服できる環境を整えてこそ、その人脈は真価を発揮する。
人脈はグラウンドの外にも広がる。ヤンキースのブライアン・キャッシュマンＧＭに加え、エンゼルス在籍時のアート・モレノ・オーナー、アスレチックス在籍時の編成トップで現上級顧問のビリー・ビーン氏。エンゼルスは球団売却で合意済みだが、人脈の幅広さは際立つ。１２年の現役最後に在籍したレイズの編成トップは、現ドジャース編成本部長のアンドリュー・フリードマン氏。こうした球団との縁が助っ人の獲得や育成、情報交換に生きない手はない。
数字では測れない選手の適応力や人柄を見極めるには、現地の情報が欠かせないはずだ。交渉はフロントの仕事でも、松井監督の助言が〝掘り出し物〟の獲得につながるかもしれない。
ＭＬＢの現行労使協定は１２月１日（日本時間２日）に失効予定。ロックアウトとなった場合、ＭＬＢは選手がその間、ＮＰＢなどでプレーすることを認める方針を各球団に通達したと報じられている。来春まで長期化すれば、超大物の一時的な来日も想定される。一方でジャッジにはヤンキースとの長期契約があり、本人の意向や球団間の調整も含めハードルは高い。それでも師弟の縁を生かしたロックアウト中の短期加入、あるいは松井監督の在任中に実現する数年先の大型補強という構想は十分に描ける。
松井監督は「今、世界一の野球選手が日本人であることも事実です」と述べ、巨人から世界に通用する選手を育てる決意を示した。巨人の理念は「アメリカ野球に追いつけ、追い越せ」――。その理想を、海の向こうで得た〝スーパーコネクション〟を武器に実現できるか。新生巨人の夢は松井新監督を発信源に東京ドームの外、世界へ広がっている。

item.content:encoded:
El Clásico de Otoño comenzará este viernes en el American Family Field, y los nombres de Carlos “Calicho” Ruiz y Mariano Rivera vuelven a destacar entre las figuras históricas del béisbol de las Grandes Ligas. Los dos panameños fueron incluidos por FOX Sports en su selección ideal de la Serie Mundial del siglo XXI, una nómina de 26 jugadores que reúne a peloteros de la Liga Americana y la Liga Nacional por sus actuaciones en el Clásico de Otoño.
Ruiz aparece como el receptor titular de la alineación, mientras que Rivera fue elegido como cerrador. La presencia de ambos en este listado reconoce el impacto que tuvieron con los Filis de Filadelfia y los Yankees de Nueva York, respectivamente, durante una época marcada por sus éxitos en la postemporada.
La selección de FOX Sports se conoce en la antesala de la Serie Mundial de 2026, que comenzará este viernes 23 de octubre con el primer partido entre los Rays de Tampa Bay y los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, en el American Family Field, a las 7:00 p. m., hora de Panamá.
Ruiz, el receptor titular
El portal deportivo destacó la actuación de Ruiz durante la etapa más exitosa de los Filis en la postemporada. El panameño fue el receptor de cinco equipos consecutivos de Filadelfia que disputaron los playoffs entre 2007 y 2011, periodo que incluyó dos apariciones consecutivas en la Serie Mundial, en 2008 y 2009.
En la edición de 2008, los Filis vencieron a los Rays en cinco partidos para conquistar el título. Durante aquella postemporada, Ruiz también registró una destacada producción ofensiva. En la Serie Mundial de 2009, Filadelfia cayó ante los Yankees de Nueva York. En ambas finales, el istmeño acumuló un promedio de bateo de .353, dos jonrones y cinco carreras impulsadas en 11 partidos.
El receptor jugó 12 temporadas en las Grandes Ligas, 11 de ellas con los Filis. También vistió los uniformes de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles y los Marineros de Seattle, equipo con el que puso fin a su carrera en 2017.
Rivera, el cerrador de la selección
En el caso de Rivera, FOX Sports resaltó su dominio como relevista en el escenario más importante del béisbol. El panameño registró una efectividad de 0.99 en 36 entradas y un tercio de labor en la Serie Mundial, una cifra que refleja su consistencia en sus apariciones en el Clásico de Otoño.
Rivera participó en siete Series Mundiales y acumuló 11 salvamentos, según las estadísticas consignadas en el texto original. Su efectividad de 0.99 en 36 entradas y un tercio lo sitúa entre los relevistas más dominantes en la historia de estas finales.
El legendario cerrador disputó 19 temporadas en las Grandes Ligas, todas con los Yankees de Nueva York, y terminó su carrera con 652 salvamentos, la mayor cantidad en la historia de las Mayores. En 2019 ingresó de manera unánime al Salón de la Fama del Béisbol.
La inclusión de Ruiz y Rivera en esta selección vuelve a poner de relieve el lugar de Panamá en la historia de las Grandes Ligas. Ambos fueron piezas determinantes en equipos campeones y dejaron una huella que trasciende sus estadísticas individuales.
Los otros 24 jugadores seleccionados por FOX Sports son Freddie Freeman, Chase Utley, David Freese, Derek Jeter, George Springer, Barry Bonds, Hideki Matsui, David Ortiz, Madison Bumgarner, Yadier Molina, Alex Rodríguez, Pablo Sandoval, Justin Turner, Corey Seager, Juan Soto, Jayson Werth, Curt Schilling, Jon Lester, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Gerrit Cole, Chris Carpenter, Josh Beckett, Walker Buehler y Tim Lincecum.

item.title: [amsterdamnews.com] Can the Yankees take down the Red Sox without Aaron Judge?
item.dc:creator: JAIME C HARRIS AmNews Sports Editor

item.content:encoded:
This was supposed to be the year the Yankees would win the franchise’s first World Series since 2009. A roster that included all-time greats Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera and Alex Rodriguez, Hall of Famer CC Sabathia, and Series MVP Hideki Matsui, one of the best players Japan has ever produced.
Yet, as the Yankees look towards Tuesday, when they open the playoffs at home against what is virtually certain to be the Boston Red Sox, their longtime nemesis, in a best-of-three wildcard series, the prospects of them navigating an always perilous path to the World Series were reduced when Yankees manager Aaron Boone said this past Tuesday that the reigning American League MVP likely won’t play in the series due to a right calf strain.
“We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone revealed to reporters.
Judge, who has only appeared in 66 games this season, primarily recovering from a right rib stress fracture, which caused him to sit out 84 games from May 31 to Sept. 8, is now on the 10-day injured list, placed there last Friday. The 34-year-old Judge, arguably the best player in the sport over the last decade, isn’t expected back for the divisional round if the Yankees get by the Red Sox.
Last weekend, Boone informed the media the team didn’t have a firm estimate as to when Judge, a three-time AL MVP, three-time AL home run leader, two-time MLB RBI king and last season’s MLB batting champion, would return to the lineup.
“I mean, I have no idea, we’re in the early stages,” expressed Boone, now in his ninth season as the Yankees manager. “We’ll just obviously treat it and see what transpires.”
The Yankees watched Tampa Bay clinch the AL East title on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium when they won the second game of a double-header on Tuesday 6-1. The Yankees shut out the Rays in the opener. Tampa Bay 96-61 going into the third game of the four-game series last night with the finale scheduled for 7:05 tonight. The Yankees were second in the division at 90-67 and the 84-73 Red Sox third.
With Judge unavailable, the Yankees offense will have to be multifaceted — both power and small ball will be required to make a deep postseason run. Designated hitter Ben Rice, who as of Wednesday had 39 home runs and 95 RBIs, both team highs, was the only Yankee with more than 20 homers and 80 runs batted in, so timely power will have to come from sources such as second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (19 home runs), first baseman Paul Goldschmidt (18), and left fielder Cody Bellinger (17).
But it is pitching that must advance the Yankees, led by leading AL Cy Young Award candidate Cam Schlittler, who is 14-6 with a 1.94 ERA and 234 strikeouts. Schlittler is scheduled to start tonight before taking the mound next week in the wildcard series.
But the prevailing question is: Can the Yankees win without Judge?

item.title: [ｄメニューニュース] 松井秀喜が全身ヒョウ柄、ダルビッシュはヘソ出しTシャツとピッタリ水着／過去のMLB新人仮装（日刊スポーツ）｜ｄメニューニュース
item.description: ブルージェイズ岡本和真内野手（30）が、MLBでは新人の恒例行事となっている仮装で遠征先のテキサスに向かった。 同球団は17日（日本時間18日）、公式インスタグラムやXで新人選手がカウボーイ姿で次々と登場する動画を公開。岡本も他の新人と同様にチェックのノースリーブのシャツに丈が短めの半ズボン、ウェスタンブーツとカウボーイハットを身に着けて登場した。動画には日本語で「俺らのカウボーイ！」とのメッセージも添えられた。 MLBで新人が仮装で移動するのは恒例の“いじり”。日本人では過去にも、松井秀喜が全身ヒョウ柄、岩村明憲がタンクトップに半ズボン、川崎宗則が背中に羽がついたチョウチョ姿（！？）、ダルビッシュ有もヘソ出しTシャツと白い水泳帽、競泳用のピッタリ水着というスタイルで“洗礼”を受けた。
item.content:encoded:
ブルージェイズ岡本和真内野手（30）が、MLBでは新人の恒例行事となっている仮装で遠征先のテキサスに向かった。
同球団は17日（日本時間18日）、公式インスタグラムやXで新人選手がカウボーイ姿で次々と登場する動画を公開。岡本も他の新人と同様にチェックのノースリーブのシャツに丈が短めの半ズボン、ウェスタンブーツとカウボーイハットを身に着けて登場した。動画には日本語で「俺らのカウボーイ！」とのメッセージも添えられた。
MLBで新人が仮装で移動するのは恒例の“いじり”。日本人では過去にも、松井秀喜が全身ヒョウ柄、岩村明憲がタンクトップに半ズボン、川崎宗則が背中に羽がついたチョウチョ姿（！？）、ダルビッシュ有もヘソ出しTシャツと白い水泳帽、競泳用のピッタリ水着というスタイルで“洗礼”を受けた。
